sentences.text: 2. Insurance Company is in appeal challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.96/2006 dated 16.11.2011 on the file of the Fast Track Court-II, Dharwad, sitting at Hubballi.

3. Facts in brief which are not in dispute for disposal of the present appeal are as under:
A road traffic accident occurred on 13.10.2005 involving a car bearing registration No.MH-15/B-6175 and a lorry bearing registration No.HR-55/0220 near Kopargaon on a highway whereby one Gajanan who was an inmate of the Car lost his life.

Dependents of said Gajanan filed claim petition which, on contest, came to be allowed in part in a sum of Rs.9,05,000/- with 6% interest per annum from the date of petition till realization, fastening the liability on the Insurance Company of the lorry to the extent of 50% and owner of the car to an extent of 50%.
The accident occurred on account of the fact that the tyre of the lorry got punctured and therefore, it was parked on the road without proper indication.

The driver of the car, not noticing the lorry parked on the road, on account of high beam light of a opposite vehicle, dashed against the lorry resulting in the death of inmate of the car-Gajanan due to grievous injuries sustained in the accident.

4. Taking note of the fact that the lorry has been parked on the highway without proper indication,
the Tribunal assessed the contributory negligence to the driver of the lorry to the extent of 50%,
though charge sheet came to be filed against the driver of the car.
Admittedly, owner of the car did not get the car insured and therefore, 50% is fastened on the owner of the car and 50% of the liability on the Insurer of the lorry.
5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, insurance company is in appeal.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contended that the approach of the Trial Court in attributing 50% to the driver of the lorry is incorrect and lorry had been parked on the NC:
2024:KHC-D:1094 road on account of the fact that the tyre got punctured and as such, driver was not in a position to move the lorry away.
7.

He also argued that since charge sheet filed against driver of the car, attributing 50% negligence to the driver of the lorry is incorrect and has resulted in miscarriage of justice and sought for allowing the appeal.
8. The first respondent claimant who is the mother of minor- respondent No.2, has engaged the services of Ahmed Ali Rahiman Shah, who remained absent at the hearing.
Other respondents are served and unrepresented.
9. In the light of the arguments putforth on behalf of the appellant, this Court perused the material on record, meticulously.

On such perusal of the material on record, it is crystal clear that the The Divisionalmanager, National ... vs Padma W/O Gajanan Gadad on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115030893/
3 accident occurred on account of the fact that lorry was parked on the highway without proper indications/caution.

sentences.text: 10. In the first place, on the highway, lorry could not have been parked.
Reason assigned by the driver for parking the lorry is that the tyre of the lorry got punctured.

In such an NC:
2024:KHC-D:1094 event, necessary precaution should have been taken by the driver and cleaner of the lorry by exhibiting reflectors and indicators so as to caution the drivers moving on the same lane that there is an obstruction for free passage of the vehicles.
11. Spot panchanama contents do not indicate that driver and cleaner of the lorry had taken such necessary precautions.

No material is placed on record in this regard before the Tribunal for establishing the fact that despite taking sufficient precautionary measures, it is the driver of the car who was at fault resulting in accidental death of Gajanan, an inmate of the car.
12. Under such circumstances, Tribunal, on cumulative analysis of the material evidence placed on record, has rightly attributed 50% contributory negligence to the driver of the lorry.
But for the obstruction found on the highway, car would not have met with accident and precious life of Gajanan would not have been lost.

13. Taking note of these aspects of the matter, this Court is of the considered opinion that the approach of the Tribunal is just and proper in the attendant facts and circumstances of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:1094 case, which requires no interference at the hands of this Court by exercising appellate powers vested with this Court.

14. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is meritless and is hereby dismissed.

(ii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement,
in accordance with law.

Sd/-
